claims.subject: work:rogaski_hygienic_2004
claims.statement: Rogaski traces changes in weisheng through imperial encounters, state power and racialized standards of modernity.
claims.qualification: Selected introduction only; retain the changing Chinese concept rather than equating it with timeless Western hygiene.

claims.subject: work:rogaski_hygienic_2004
claims.statement: Rogaski uses Tianjin to connect bodily practice, the built environment and projects of national modernity.
claims.qualification: Introduction pp. 1–3; one treaty-port inquiry, not a proxy for all Chinese or Asian medical historiography.

claims.subject: work:cueto_palmer_medicine
claims.statement: Cueto and Palmer situate Latin American and Caribbean health histories within social and cultural history and science-and-technology studies.
claims.qualification: Publisher chapter summary only; detailed arguments about medical pluralism and local innovation still require body-text verification.
claims.locator: Publisher Introduction summary, opening two paragraphs

claims.subject: work:cooper_owens_bondage_2017
claims.statement: Cooper Owens places enslaved Black women and Irish immigrant women within the history of American gynecology and its racialized medical assumptions.
claims.qualification: Publisher description only. Do not infer voluntary participation, homogeneous experiences, or a checked reconstruction of individual patients.

claims.subject: work:mccallum_health_2017
claims.statement: McCallum examines how scholarship on starvation, experimentation, segregation and trauma sharpens the analysis of colonialism in Canadian Indigenous health history.
claims.qualification: Author abstract only; this is a historiographical framing, not new clinical evidence or a universal model of Indigenous experience.
claims.locator: Author abstract reproduced on ResearchGate; publisher body unavailable

claims.subject: work:wynter_et_al_persistence_2025
claims.statement: Wynter, Campbell, Chaney and Marks historicize changing explanations of mental illness while tracing the persistence of racialized assumptions.
claims.qualification: Version-of-record opening pp. 2–3 checked; attribution to this historical analysis, not clinical guidance or endorsement of historical racial categories.
claims.locator: Version of record, article pp. 2–3 (PDF pp. 3–4), lines 88–135

claims.subject: work:wynter_et_al_persistence_2025
claims.statement: Wynter and coauthors widen the history of antiracist psychiatry by examining Frederick Hickling, Aggrey Burke and Suman Fernando alongside better-known figures.
claims.qualification: Selected programme passage pp. 2–3; clinicians are subjects of the 2025 study, not its coauthors. Their careers are not dated 2025.
claims.locator: Version of record, article pp. 2–3 (PDF pp. 3–4), lines 88–135

claims.subject: work:harris_native_space_2002
claims.statement: Harris reads competing colonial land policies as spatial arrangements with different consequences for Indigenous lives.
claims.qualification: Publisher chapter pp. 8–10 only; analysis of Merivale and imperial policy is not Indigenous testimony or an exhaustive account of Indigenous territorial knowledge.
claims.locator: Publisher sample chapter, The Imperial Background, printed pp. 8–10; extracted lines 168–250

claims.subject: work:mckittrick_demonic_2006
claims.statement: McKittrick treats racial and sexual domination as spatial processes while preserving Black women’s geographic knowledge and contestation.
claims.qualification: Chapter 5 pp. 121–123 only, read in the authorized 2020 reprint. Not a new 2020 programme or a whole-book reading.
claims.locator: Chapter 5, original printed pp. 121–123, in 2020 authorized reprint; PDF pp. 4–6

claims.subject: work:mckittrick_demonic_2006
claims.statement: McKittrick explicitly develops a geographic reading of Sylvia Wynter’s critique of the overrepresentation of Man.
claims.qualification: Chapter 5 pp. 122–123; bounded account of her stated use of Wynter. No generalized genealogy or claim of first reception.
claims.locator: Original printed pp. 122–123, reprint PDF pp. 5–6; lines 131–187

claims.subject: work:gregory_healey_hgis_2007
claims.statement: Gregory and Healey describe historical GIS as extending from quantitative into qualitative inquiry and across disciplinary boundaries.
claims.qualification: Author abstract only; GIS is one method within historical geography, not its beginning or its synonym.
claims.locator: Author-deposited abstract; repository explicitly has no full text

claims.subject: work:machado_gomes_geografia_2013
claims.statement: Machado and Gomes distinguish Abreu’s urban-historical work from Moraes’s inquiries into geopolitics and territorial management in Brazilian historical geography.
claims.qualification: Portuguese abstract read; English research paraphrase. Their two examples do not exhaust Brazilian scholarship or establish unique founders.
claims.locator: Portuguese Resumo in indexed primary journal record

claims.subject: work:silveira_brazil_2024
claims.statement: Gomes da Silveira calls for historical geography to include Brazilian and other southern sites of knowledge production beyond an English-speaking canon.
claims.qualification: Indexed publisher abstract only; named networks and institutional history require body-text review. Regional coverage remains partial.

claims.subject: work:legg_et_al_translation_2025
claims.statement: Legg and coauthors propose multilingual reviews and reflection on translation to broaden historical geography’s disciplinary conversation.
claims.qualification: Editorial pp. 5–6; proposed journal practice, not evidence of completed decolonization. All five author credits preserved.
claims.locator: Journal of Historical Geography 88, pp. 5–6, opening and translation discussion

claims.subject: work:lovejoy_diaspora_1997
claims.statement: Lovejoy proposes reconstructing African backgrounds in diaspora history through historically specific identities, biographies, oral sources and movements.
claims.qualification: Indexed author abstract only; neither an undifferentiated African cultural survival nor an unchanging ethnic identity is inferred.
claims.locator: Indexed abstract of university-hosted original article, first page

claims.subject: work:lovejoy_jihad_2016
claims.statement: Lovejoy argues for placing West African jihād movements within wider histories of the age of revolutions and the Atlantic world.
claims.qualification: Publisher description only; interpretation is attributed to the book, with body-text and independent reception review pending.
claims.locator: Ohio University Press Description, first paragraph

claims.subject: work:eley_crooked_2005
claims.statement: Eley’s intellectual autobiography follows social history through the cultural turn toward a renewed history of society.
claims.qualification: Publisher description only; supports a proposed social-history connection without reducing Eley to one school or removing his Sonderweg critique.

claims.subject: work:eley_nield_class_2007
claims.statement: Eley and Nield examine class to develop collaboration between social and cultural historical approaches.
claims.qualification: Publisher description only; coauthored argument, not a rejection of cultural history or an exclusively Eley contribution.
claims.locator: Publisher Description paragraph, not endorsement quotations
